name: Conus medullaris
summary: The tapered lower end of the spinal cord, containing the sacral segments (S2–S5 and coccygeal), ending at the L1–L2 disc level in most adults, from which the filum terminale continues to the coccyx. It houses the sacral parasympathetic nucleus and Onuf's nucleus, so its lesions produce early, symmetric sphincter failure and saddle anesthesia with relatively little leg weakness, the conus syndrome, which must be distinguished from the asymmetric, painful, lower motor neuron cauda equina syndrome affecting the roots below it.

anatomy.location: Lower border of L1 to the L1–L2 disc in most adults (range T12–L3), surrounded by the emerging lumbar and sacral roots of the cauda equina; the level is fixed by the age of two years.

function: Contains the sacral segments: parasympathetic outflow to the bladder, rectum and genitals, motor neurons for the pelvic floor and sphincters, and sensory relay for the perineum.

bestView.label: cord (the conus lies at L1–L2, below the MNI volume)

imaging.normalAppearance: On sagittal lumbar MRI the conus should end at or above L2; a low-lying conus with a thick filum indicates tethering. Conus lesions (ependymoma, infarct, myelitis) appear as focal signal change or expansion of the cone.

pathology.finding: T2 hyperintensity and restricted diffusion of the conus after aortic surgery or in vascular malformations.
Conus below L2 with a thickened filum or lipoma.
Enhancing mass of the conus and filum with hemorrhage.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Sagittal and axial lumbar T2 and T1+Gd; DWI

lesionEffects.deficit: Early urinary retention and fecal incontinence
Mild, symmetric leg weakness with mixed reflexes (brisk knee, absent ankle)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Sacral segments and adjacent lumbar tracts

examination: Perianal pin-prick, anal tone and reflex, bulbocavernosus reflex
pearls: Sphincters first, symmetric and painless: conus. Legs first, asymmetric and painful: cauda equina
The conus is at L1–L2: a lumbar puncture at L3–L4 or below is safe

pitfalls: PUBLIC EDITION - VERTEBRAL-LANDMARK CUT: the two surfaces this entry lights up are cut at PAM50 spinal-level boundaries, which the openly shareable build may not redistribute, so it shows the vertebral-landmark cut of the same Z-Anatomy cord instead. There the conus tip is the middle of the model's own L1-L2 intervertebral disc -- the classical adult level, a textbook rule rather than a measurement on this specimen -- so the junction between the sacral block and the filum marks roughly, not exactly, where the cord ends.
